I still fall with my previous answer and believe that money used to directly benefit the community (giveaways, etc.) would be more beneficial to the growth of FPH rather than a 7-day ad, at this stage at least. FPH is the majority of voat, most users have made their decision about joining. If/When voat becomes larger an ad will introduce unknown users to the community, but for now you can increase the "potential value" of being an FPH member and this will serve as a catalyst to people joining and experiencing the community.

The purchasing of the ad assumes there is a large population base on voat unaware of FPH, I highly doubt that this a significant percentage of the userbase (I wish we had numbers, although I do imagine there is a small number of those users). By this assumption we can split the voat community into 4 groups:

  1. Those who have joined FPH
  2. Those who have rejected FPH
  3. Those unsure if they want to commit to FPH
  4. Those unaware of FPH

As voat is a small community my contention is that trying to make group 4 aware of FPH will have a significantly weaker impact than directing your efforts to group 3 as group 4 is significantly smaller. This comes down to a numbers game, who do you think is a larger untapped base, group 3 or group 4? Without rigid numbers we need to assess what we know: The banning of FPH led to the influx on voat and voat remains a small community, therefore nearly all of the users know of FPH and if they do not FPH posts are consistently on the front page.

Having giveaways/contests will also appear on the front page and aside from rewarding current members, it will show non-member users the interaction and strength of the community. An ad may be the best option in a few years, but I think now it is not the most effective in recruiting members and strengthening the community.

A retort would be that you do not want people joining for free things, but that can be solved with a simple restriction that users must have posted prior to a contest beginning.

Contests and giveaways may not be the best method for growing FPH, but I think is more valuable than the ad, I think the ad will be very ineffective and a monetary infusion can be better utilized to grow the community.

Anyone have tips for increasing running endurance? My lungs are shit (doctors have no clue what's up with my breathing problems over the past couple of years) and I can slowly increase how far I run, but if I take more than two days off from jogging, I lose all of my progress and have to start over at square one.

Well, eveyone is different as to what works for them. Back when I took my running much more seriously, I was mostly doing uphill circuit sprints interspersed at about three quarters into any given training run. Things have moved on a bit since then though.

It sounds like you might benefit from wiki: plyometrics to make the legs work better for you, those developments should give you progress despite the limitations of lungs you mentioned...

"We started with core strength, and progressed to explosive leg plyometrics, always focusing on the basics, and doing quality sessions, not quantity. Runners already do enough quantity," he says. "In her first plyometrics workouts, Deena hit the ground like this big, flat-footed person, but we kept emphasizing, 'Get your feet up fast. Get your feet up fast.'"

Looking back, I used to do some of this, not knowing the posh term... it was mainly just skipping really!

These days I'm happy with my endurance levels as I just run different routes for the variety and fitness with no real competition or end goal in mind. But I'd happily pick up a skipping rope again I suppose. Hmm, maybe I might get another one because I've no idea where my old one is. This has certainly planted an idea in my head.

When I did endurance running what I would do is make running as uncomfortable as possible to make comfortable running much easier. I'd run with a weighted vest or run on an empty stomach. Sometimes I'd run very, very early in the morning or late at night when it's really cold because it forces you to be more efficient with your breathing.

Breathe through your nose while you run.

The biggest thing with running though is will power. It's a lot more mental than it is something you need to work up to.

I was terrible until I went minimalist. Then after pain helped correct my gait, it became much more efficient and easy.

I can do a sub 2 hour half without training now, just by falling back into my gait. (Not impressive I know, but its damn good for zero training and no nutrition work)
